## [Model availability & compatibility](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/models.md)

- [API compatibility by models](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/models-api-compatibility.md): Amazon Bedrock supports four families of runtime APIs, each designed for different integration patterns and use cases.
- [Endpoint availability by models](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/models-endpoint-availability.md): Amazon Bedrock supports two endpoints: bedrock-runtime and bedrock-mantle.
- [Regional availability by models](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/models-region-compatibility.md): Amazon Bedrock gives you three options so you can match the routing behavior of your inference calls to the scale, compliance, and cost requirements of your workload.
- [Regional availability by endpoints](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/endpoints-region-availability.md): The following tables show which AWS Regions support each Amazon Bedrock inference endpoint, organized by geography.
- [Get list of models](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/models-get-info.md): Amazon Bedrock provides two separate inference endpoints, each with its own API for listing the models available on it.
- [Model lifecycle](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-lifecycle.md): Learn how the model lifecycle works with Amazon Bedrock.
- [Request access to models](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-access.md): Learn how to add, manage, and remove model access to Amazon Bedrock base and custom models.
- [Subscribe from Marketplace](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-access-product-ids.md): See a list of product ID condition keys to control access to some Amazon Bedrock serverless foundation models.


## [Build](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/build.md)

- [Endpoints](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/endpoints.md): Amazon Bedrock supports various endpoints for performing inference operations.
- [APIs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/apis.md): Inference APIs supported

### [Making inference requests](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/inference.md)

Learn how to make inference requests to foundation models in Amazon Bedrock to generate text, images, and embeddings.

- [Responses API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/bedrock-mantle.md): Learn how to use the OpenAI Responses API with Amazon Bedrock to generate responses from foundation models.
- [Chat Completions API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/inference-chat-completions-mantle.md): Learn how to use the OpenAI Chat Completions API with Amazon Bedrock to generate conversational responses from foundation models.

### [Messages API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/inference-messages-api.md)

Learn how to use the Anthropic Messages API with Amazon Bedrock to generate responses from Claude models.

- [Extended thinking](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/claude-messages-extended-thinking.md): Learn how to use Anthropic Claude's extended thinking capabilities for complex reasoning tasks, with step-by-step thought processes and enhanced problem-solving abilities.
- [Adaptive thinking](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/claude-messages-adaptive-thinking.md): Learn how to use Anthropic Claude's adaptive thinking capabilities, which dynamically decides when and how much to think based on request complexity.
- [Compaction](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/claude-messages-compaction.md): Learn how to use Anthropic Claude's compaction feature to automatically summarize context in long-running conversations and agentic workflows.
- [Fallback credit for refused requests (beta)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/claude-messages-fallback-credit.md): When Claude Fable 5 refuses a request, customers who retry the same conversation on a different model (such as Claude Opus 4.8) normally re-pay cache-write rates for the conversation prefix that was already cached on Fable 5.
- [Mid-conversation system messages](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/claude-messages-mid-conversation-system.md): Learn how to use mid-conversation system messages to add or update system instructions partway through a conversation.
- [Invoke API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/inference-api.md): Learn how to programmatically interact with Amazon Bedrock foundation models using API operations to generate text, images, and embeddings for your applications.
- [Converse API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/conversation-inference.md): Learn how to build conversational AI applications using the Amazon Bedrock Converse API to manage multi-turn dialogues with foundation models.
- [Inference parameters](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/inference-parameters.md): Learn how to control and customize foundation model outputs by adjusting inference parameters like temperature, top_p, and max_tokens in Amazon Bedrock.
- [Structured Outputs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/structured-output.md): Structured outputs is a capability in Amazon Bedrock that ensures model responses conform to user-defined JSON schemas and tool definitions, reducing the need for custom parsing and validation mechanisms in production AI deployments.
- [Inference reasoning](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/inference-reasoning.md): Learn how to improve foundation model accuracy and transparency by using chain of thought reasoning to break down complex tasks into simpler steps.
- [Latency-optimized inference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/latency-optimized-inference.md): Learn how to reduce response times and improve user experience by using latency-optimized inference for Amazon Bedrock foundation models.
- [Supported Regions and models](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/inference-supported.md): The content from this page has moved.

### [Tool use](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/tool-use.md)

Shows how to call a tool (function) with Amazon Bedrock Tool Use (Function Calling).

- [Client-side](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/tool-use-client-side.md): If you use the Responses API, Chat Completions API, Converse API, or InvokeModel API to send the request, then the model uses client-side tool calling.
- [Server-side](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/tool-use-server-side.md): If you use the Responses API to invoke the model, then it can use server-side tool calling, in addition to the client-side tool calling we discussed before.
- [Anthropic Claude tool use](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-parameters-anthropic-claude-messages-tool-use.md): Learn how to use Anthropic Claude models with tools to enhance responses and automate tasks through API integration.
- [Projects](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/projects.md): Amazon Bedrock Projects API provides application-level isolation for your generative AI workloads using OpenAI-compatible APIs.
- [Workspaces](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/workspaces.md): Learn how to use Amazon Bedrock Workspaces to isolate generative AI workloads, track costs, and enforce access control when using the Anthropic Messages API on the bedrock-mantle endpoint.
- [API keys](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/api-keys.md): Generate and use Amazon Bedrock API keys to authenticate API requests without configuring AWS credentials.


## [Model customization](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/custom-models.md)

### [Supervised fine-tuning](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/custom-model-fine-tuning.md)

With Amazon Bedrock, you can train a foundation model to improve performance on specific tasks (known as fine-tuning).

- [Prepare data for fine-tuning your models](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-customization-prepare.md): Learn how to prepare training datasets for different types of models and customization approaches in Amazon Bedrock.
- [Fine-tune Amazon Nova models](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/nova-2-sft-data-prep.md): Amazon Nova 2.0 SFT data uses the same Converse API format as Amazon Nova 1.0, with the addition of optional reasoning content fields.
- [Custom model hyperparameters](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/custom-models-hp.md): Learn about the hyperparameters available for customizing foundation models in Amazon Bedrock, including settings for learning rate, batch size, and epochs.
- [Submit a model fine-tuning job](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-customization-submit.md): You can create a custom model by using fine-tuning in the Amazon Bedrock console or API.

Learn how to use reinforcement fine-tuning to improve foundation model performance through feedback signals.

- [Create fine-tuning jobs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/rft-submit-job.md): Learn how to create and submit a reinforcement fine-tuning job using the console or API, and how to monitor the job's progress, and gather metrics.

## [Security, Guardrails, and Observability](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/security.md)

### [Security](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/security-overview.md)

Learn about security features and best practices for Amazon Bedrock.

### [Data protection](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/data-protection.md)

Learn how the AWS shared responsibility model applies to data protection in Amazon Bedrock.

### [Data encryption](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/data-encryption.md)

Amazon Bedrock uses encryption to protect data at rest and data in transit.

- [Encryption of custom models](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/encryption-custom-job.md): Amazon Bedrock uses your training data with the CreateModelCustomizationJob action, or with the console, to create a custom model which is a fine tuned version of an Amazon Bedrock foundational model.

### [Encryption of imported custom models](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/encryption-import-model.md)

Amazon Bedrock supports creating custom models through two methods that both use the same encryption approach.

- [Using customer managed key (CMK)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/import-model-using-cmk.md): If you are planning to use customer managed key to encrypt your custom imported model, complete the following steps:
- [Monitoring your encryption keys for the Amazon Bedrock service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/import-model-monitor-encryption-keys.md): When you use an AWS KMS customer managed key with your Amazon Bedrock resources, you can use AWS CloudTrail or Amazon CloudWatch Logs to track requests that Amazon Bedrock sends to AWS KMS.
- [Encryption in Amazon Bedrock Data Automation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/encryption-bda.md): Amazon Bedrock Data Automation (BDA) uses encryption to protect your data at rest.

### [Encryption of agent resources](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/encryption-agents-new.md)

Encryption of data at rest by default helps reduce the operational overhead and complexity involved in protecting sensitive data.

### [Encryption of agent resources with customer managed keys (CMK)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/cmk-agent-resources.md)

You can at any time create a customer managed key to encrypt your agent’s information using the following agent information provided when building your agent.

- [Encrypt agent sessions with customer managed key (CMK)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/ltm-permissions.md): If you've enabled memory for your agent and if you encrypt agent sessions with a customer managed key, you must configure the following key policy and the calling identity IAM permissions to configure your customer managed key.
- [Preventative security best practice for agents](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/security-best-practice-agents.md): The following best practices for Amazon Bedrock service can help prevent security incidents:
- [Encryption of agent resources for agents created before January 22, 2025](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/encryption-agents.md)
- [Encryption of flow resources](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/encryption-flows.md): Amazon Bedrock encrypts your data at rest.
- [Encryption of knowledge base resources](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/encryption-kb.md): Amazon Bedrock encrypts resources related to your knowledge bases.

### [Protect your data using a Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/usingVPC.md)

- [Agents service role](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/agents-permissions.md): To use a custom service role for agents instead of the one Amazon Bedrock automatically creates, create an IAM role and attach the following permissions by following the steps at Creating a role to delegate permissions to an AWS service.
- [Knowledge base service role](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-permissions.md): To use a custom role for a knowledge base instead of the one Amazon Bedrock automatically creates, create an IAM role and attach the following permissions by following the steps at Creating a role to delegate permissions to an AWS service.
- [Amazon Bedrock Flows service role](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/flows-permissions.md): To create and manage a flow in Amazon Bedrock, you must use a service role with the necessary permissions outlined on this page.

- [Infrastructure security](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/infrastructure-security.md): Learn how Amazon Bedrock isolates service traffic.
- [Cross-service confused deputy prevention](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/cross-service-confused-deputy-prevention.md): The confused deputy problem is a security issue where an entity that doesn't have permission to perform an action can coerce a more-privileged entity to perform the action.
- [Configuration and vulnerability analysis in Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/vulnerability-analysis-and-management.md): Configuration and IT controls are a shared responsibility between AWS and you, our customer.
- [Abuse detection](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/abuse-detection.md): Learn about Amazon Bedrock automated abuse detection mechanisms that help prevent misuse and identify potential violations of acceptable use policies.
- [Prompt injection security](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-injection.md): As per the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, AWS is responsible for securing the underlying cloud infrastructure, including the hardware, software, networking, and facilities that run AWS services.

### [Bedrock Guardrails](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails.md)

Learn how to reduce and protect from harmful information being sent to end-users.

- [Overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails-how.md): Guardrails helps block harmful content using word and image filters, policies, and contextual grounding checks.
- [Supported Regions/models](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails-supported.md): Learn about AWS Region and model support for Amazon Bedrock Guardrails.
- [Safeguard tiers for guardrails policies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails-tiers.md): Amazon Bedrock Guardrails provides safeguard tiers for specific policies.
- [Supported languages](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails-supported-languages.md): Learn which languages are supported by Amazon Bedrock Guardrails.
- [Prerequisites](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails-prereq.md): Learn the prerequisites for using Amazon Bedrock Guardrails and what you should prepare to create a guardrail.

### [Set up permissions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails-permissions.md)

Learn how to configure the necessary IAM permissions and roles to create, manage, and use Amazon Bedrock guardrails for content filtering.

- [Permissions for Automated Reasoning policies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrail-automated-reasoning-permissions.md): Learn what IAM permissions you need to use Automated Reasoning policies with the ApplyGuardrail API.
- [Permissions for Automated Reasoning with agents](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrail-automated-reasoning-agent-permissions.md): Learn what additional IAM permissions you need to use Automated Reasoning policies with Amazon Bedrock agents.
- [(Optional) Permissions for encrypting a guardrail](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails-permissions-kms.md): You encrypt your guardrails with customer managed AWS KMS keys.
- [Enforce specific guardrails during inference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails-permissions-id.md): You can enforce the use of a specific guardrail for model inference by including the bedrock:GuardrailIdentifier condition key in your IAM policy.
- [Permissions for using cross-Region inference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrail-profiles-permissions.md): Learn what IAM permissions you need to use cross-Region guardrail inference with Amazon Bedrock.
- [Using resource-based policies for guardrails](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails-resource-based-policies.md): Learn how to use resource-based policies to control access to Guardrails resources across accounts and organizations.

### [Create your guardrail](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails-components.md)

Learn about the different filters and blockers of a guardrail in Amazon Bedrock

### [Configure content filters](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails-content-filters-overview.md)

With Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, you can configure content filters to block model prompts and responses in natural language for text and images containing harmful content.

- [Content filters (text)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails-content-filters.md): Amazon Bedrock Guardrails supports content filters to help detect and filter harmful user inputs and model-generated outputs in natural language as well as code-related content in Standard tier.
- [Content filters (images)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails-mmfilter.md): Learn how to use Amazon Bedrock guardrails to detect and filter harmful image content in multimodal AI applications.
- [Prompt attacks](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails-prompt-attack.md): Learn how prompt attacks work and the different types of prompt attacks.
- [Add denied topics](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails-denied-topics.md): You can specify a set of denied topics in a guardrail that are undesirable in the context of your generative AI application.
- [Add word filters](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails-word-filters.md): Amazon Bedrock Guardrails has word filters that you can use to block words and phrases (exact match) in input prompts and model responses.
- [Add sensitive information filters](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails-sensitive-filters.md): Amazon Bedrock Guardrails helps detect sensitive information, such as personally identifiable information (PII), in input prompts or model responses using sensitive information filters.
- [Add contextual grounding checks](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails-contextual-grounding-check.md): Amazon Bedrock Guardrails supports contextual grounding checks to detect and filter hallucinations in model responses when a reference source and a user query is provided.
- [Options for handling harmful content](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails-harmful-content-handling-options.md): Learn about options for handling harmful content detected by Amazon Bedrock Guardrails.

### [What are Automated Reasoning checks?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails-automated-reasoning-checks.md)

Learn how Automated Reasoning checks in Amazon Bedrock Guardrails use mathematical verification to detect hallucinations, highlight unstated assumptions, and provide explanations for why accurate statements are correct.

- [Automated Reasoning checks concepts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/automated-reasoning-checks-concepts.md): Understand the core concepts behind Automated Reasoning checks in Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, including policies, rules, variables, custom types, findings, translation, and confidence thresholds.
- [Create your Automated Reasoning policy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/create-automated-reasoning-policy.md): Learn how to create an Automated Reasoning policy for Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, from preparing your source document through reviewing the extracted policy.
- [Policy best practices](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/automated-reasoning-policy-best-practices.md): Best practices for writing effective Automated Reasoning policies, including rule structure, variable descriptions, naming conventions, and common anti-patterns to avoid.
- [Test an Automated Reasoning policy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/test-automated-reasoning-policy.md): Learn how to test your Automated Reasoning policy using generated scenarios and QnA tests, run tests, and interpret the results before deploying to production.
- [Troubleshoot and refine your policy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/address-failed-automated-reasoning-tests.md): Learn how to diagnose and fix issues when your Automated Reasoning policy tests fail, including a systematic debugging workflow, translation fixes, rule fixes, annotations, and the quality report.
- [Use Kiro CLI with an Automated Reasoning policy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kiro-cli-automated-reasoning-policy.md): Learn how to use Kiro CLI to create, inspect, test, and refine Automated Reasoning policies using an interactive chat interface.
- [Deploy your Automated Reasoning policy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/deploy-automated-reasoning-policy.md): Learn how to save a version of your Automated Reasoning policy, add it to a guardrail, automate deployment with CloudFormation, and integrate policy deployment into CI/CD pipelines.
- [Integrate Automated Reasoning checks](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/integrate-automated-reasoning-checks.md): Learn how to use Automated Reasoning checks at runtime to validate LLM responses, interpret findings programmatically, rewrite invalid responses using Automated Reasoning feedback, ask clarifying questions, and build an audit trail.
- [Code domain support](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails-code-domain.md): Guardrails now detect and filter harmful content across both natural-language and code-related inputs and outputs.

### [Cross-Region inference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails-cross-region.md)

Learn how to improve guardrail performance by distributing inference requests across multiple AWS Regions.

- [Supported Regions for cross-Region guardrail inference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails-cross-region-support.md): Cross-Region inference with Amazon Bedrock Guardrails lets you seamlessly manage unplanned traffic bursts by using compute across different AWS Regions for your guardrail policy evaluations.
- [Cross-account safeguards](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails-enforcements.md): Learn how to automatically apply safety controls at an AWS account level and at an AWS Organizations level for all model invocations with Amazon Bedrock using guardrails enforcements.

- [View information about your guardrails](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails-view.md): Learn how to access and review details about your Amazon Bedrock guardrails, including configurations, versions, and deployment status.
- [Modify your guardrail](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails-edit.md): Learn how to update and refine your Amazon Bedrock guardrail configurations to improve content filtering effectiveness and adapt to changing requirements.
- [Delete your guardrail](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails-delete.md): Learn how to safely remove Amazon Bedrock guardrails that are no longer needed while ensuring proper cleanup of associated resources.

### [Batch inference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/batch-inference.md)

### [Prerequisites](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/batch-inference-prereq.md)

To perform batch inference, you must fulfill the following prerequisites:

- [Set up data](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/batch-inference-data.md): You must add your batch inference data to an S3 location that you'll choose or specify when submitting a model invocation job.
- [Permissions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/batch-inference-permissions.md): To carry out batch inference, you must set up permissions for the following IAM identities:
- [[Optional] Set up a VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/batch-vpc.md): Learn about using virtual private clouds to protect your batch inference data.
- [Create a job](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/batch-inference-create.md): After you've set up an Amazon S3 bucket with files for running model inference, you can create a batch inference job.
- [Monitor jobs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/batch-inference-monitor.md): Learn how to view information about a batch inference job
- [Stop a job](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/batch-inference-stop.md): Learn how to stop a batch inference job
- [View the results of a job](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/batch-inference-results.md): After a batch inference job is Completed, you can extract the results of the batch inference job from the files in the Amazon S3 bucket that you specified during creation of the job.
- [Code example](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/batch-inference-example.md): The code example in this chapter shows how to create a batch inference job, view information about it, and stop it.
- [Use the OpenAI Batch API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/inference-openai-batch.md): You can run a batch inference job using the OpenAI Create batch API with Amazon Bedrock OpenAI models.

### [Cross-Region inference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/cross-region-inference.md)

Learn how to use cross-Region inference to increase throughput of your model requests.

- [Geographic cross-Region inference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/geographic-cross-region-inference.md): Geographic cross-Region inference keeps data processing within specified geographic boundaries (US, EU, APAC, etc.) while providing higher throughput than single-region inference.
- [Global cross-Region inference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/global-cross-region-inference.md): Global cross-Region inference extends cross-Region inference beyond geographic boundaries, enabling the routing of inference requests to supported commercial AWS Regions worldwide, optimizing available resources and enabling higher model throughput.

## [Additional Capabilities](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/additional-capabilities.md)

### [Optimize and migrate prompts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-optimization-migration.md)

Optimize your prompts for model migration or improved performance using simple rewriting or evaluation-driven iterative optimization across multiple models.

- [How it works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/advanced-prompt-optimization-how.md): Learn how Advanced Prompt Optimization iteratively optimizes your prompts using evaluation-driven feedback loops.
- [Prerequisites and permissions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/advanced-prompt-optimization-prereqs.md): Learn about the IAM permissions and prerequisites needed to use Advanced Prompt Optimization.
- [Prepare your input dataset](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/advanced-prompt-optimization-input.md): Learn how to format your input JSONL file for Advanced Prompt Optimization.
- [Create and manage jobs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/advanced-prompt-optimization-jobs.md): Learn how to create, monitor, stop, and delete Advanced Prompt Optimization jobs.
- [Define evaluation methods](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/advanced-prompt-optimization-evaluation.md): Learn how to define evaluation methods for Advanced Prompt Optimization including steering criteria, LLM-as-a-judge, and custom Lambda evaluators.
- [View and interpret results](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/advanced-prompt-optimization-results.md): Learn how to access and interpret Advanced Prompt Optimization job results.
- [Regions, models, and quotas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/advanced-prompt-optimization-quotas.md): Learn about supported Regions, models, and service quotas for Advanced Prompt Optimization.
- [Troubleshooting](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/advanced-prompt-optimization-troubleshooting.md): Troubleshoot common errors with Advanced Prompt Optimization.
- [Advanced topics and strategies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/advanced-prompt-optimization-advanced-topics.md): Learn advanced strategies for multi-objective optimization and multi-turn prompt optimization with Advanced Prompt Optimization.

Learn how to customize how your data source is ingested into a knowledge base.

- [Content chunking](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-chunking.md): When ingesting your data, Amazon Bedrock first splits your documents or content into manageable chunks for efficient data retrieval.
- [Parsing options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-advanced-parsing.md): Parsing refers to the understanding and extraction of content from raw data.
- [Use a Lambda function for data ingestion](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-custom-transformation.md): You have the ability to define a custom transformation Lambda function to inject your own logic into the knowledge base ingestion process.
- [Include metadata in a data source](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-metadata.md): When ingesting CSV (comma separate values) files, you have the ability to have the knowledge base treat certain columns as content fields versus metadata fields.
- [Supported models and Regions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/knowledge-base-supported.md): Use vector embedding and generative AI models with Amazon Bedrock knowledge bases and selects your Region.
- [Chat with your document with zero setup](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/knowledge-base-chatdoc.md): Learn how to test play an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base without the need to configure a knowledge base.
- [Set up permissions to create and manage knowledge bases](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/knowledge-base-prereq-permissions-general.md): For a user or role to perform actions related to Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases, you must attach policies to it that grant permissions to perform the actions.

Connect a Confluence data source to your managed Amazon Bedrock knowledge base.

- [Set up Basic authentication](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-managed-confluence-basic-setup.md): Generate an Atlassian API token and store the credentials in AWS so your Confluence data source can crawl content.
- [Set up OAuth 2.0 authentication](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-managed-confluence-oauth2-setup.md): Register an Atlassian OAuth 2.0 (3LO) app, complete the authorization flow to get an access token and refresh token, and store the credentials in AWS.
- [Connect a data source](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-managed-ds-confluence-connect.md): Create a Confluence data source in your managed Amazon Bedrock knowledge base by using the console or the API.
- [Document-level access controls](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-managed-ds-confluence-acl.md): Enable document-level access control (ACL awareness) for a Confluence data source in a Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base.

### [Custom](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-managed-ds-custom.md)

Connect a custom data source to your managed Amazon Bedrock knowledge base.

- [Document-level access controls](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-managed-ds-custom-acl.md): Enable document-level access control (ACL awareness) for a custom data source in a Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base.

### [Google Drive](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-managed-ds-googledrive.md)

Connect a Google Drive data source to your managed Amazon Bedrock knowledge base.

- [Set up service account authentication](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-managed-googledrive-service-account-setup.md): Create a Google Cloud service account with domain-wide delegation, create a dedicated admin user for the service account to impersonate, and store the resulting credentials in AWS.
- [Set up OAuth 2.0 authentication](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-managed-googledrive-oauth2-setup.md): Create OAuth 2.0 credentials in Google Cloud, complete a sign-in flow to obtain a refresh token, and store the credentials in AWS.
- [Connect a data source](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-managed-ds-googledrive-connect.md): Create a Google Drive data source in your managed Amazon Bedrock knowledge base by using the console or the API.
- [Document-level access controls](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-managed-ds-googledrive-acl.md): Enable document-level access control (ACL awareness) for a Google Drive data source in a Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base.

### [Microsoft OneDrive](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-managed-ds-onedrive.md)

Connect a Microsoft OneDrive data source to your managed Amazon Bedrock knowledge base.

- [Set up Entra App ID authentication](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-managed-onedrive-entra-setup.md): Register a Microsoft Entra ID application, grant it the right permissions, store its client ID and secret in AWS, and (for document-level access control) add a certificate so your OneDrive data source can crawl content and verify access.
- [Set up OAuth 2.0 authentication](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-managed-onedrive-oauth2-setup.md): Register a Microsoft Entra ID application, obtain a delegated refresh token, and store OAuth 2.0 credentials in AWS so your OneDrive data source can crawl content.
- [Connect a data source](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-managed-ds-onedrive-connect.md): Create a OneDrive data source in your managed Amazon Bedrock knowledge base by using the console or the API.
- [Document-level access controls](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-managed-ds-onedrive-acl.md): Enable document-level access control (ACL awareness) for a OneDrive data source in a Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base.
- [Troubleshooting](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-managed-ds-onedrive-troubleshooting.md): Diagnose and resolve common issues with a OneDrive data source for a managed Amazon Bedrock knowledge base.

### [Microsoft SharePoint](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-managed-ds-sharepoint.md)

Connect a Microsoft SharePoint data source to your managed Amazon Bedrock knowledge base.

- [Set up Entra ID App-Only authentication](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-managed-sharepoint-entra-setup.md): Register a Microsoft Entra ID application, grant it the right permissions, generate an authentication certificate, and store the resulting credentials in AWS so your SharePoint data source can crawl content and (optionally) enforce document-level access control.
- [Set up OAuth 2.0 authentication](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-managed-sharepoint-oauth2-setup.md): Register a Microsoft Entra ID application and store OAuth 2.0 credentials in AWS so your SharePoint data source can crawl content.
- [Connect a data source](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-managed-ds-sharepoint-connect.md): Create a SharePoint data source in your managed Amazon Bedrock knowledge base by using the console or the API.
- [Document-level access controls](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-managed-ds-sharepoint-acl.md): Enable document-level access control (ACL awareness) for a SharePoint data source in a Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base.
- [Troubleshooting](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-managed-ds-sharepoint-troubleshooting.md): Diagnose and resolve common issues with a SharePoint data source for a managed Amazon Bedrock knowledge base.
- [Web Crawler](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-managed-ds-webcrawler.md): Connect a Web Crawler data source to your managed Amazon Bedrock knowledge base.

- [Sync a data source](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-managed-sync.md): Learn how to sync your data source and ingest your data into your managed knowledge base.
- [View information about a data source](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-managed-ds-info.md): Learn how to view important information about a data source for a managed Amazon Bedrock knowledge base, such as the current settings and sync history.
- [ACL awareness enablement](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-managed-acl.md): Understand how access control list (ACL) awareness works in a Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base, what it does and does not guarantee, and the responsibilities you take on when you enable it.
- [Resource policies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-managed-cross-account.md): Use resource-based policies to control access to your managed Amazon Bedrock knowledge base.
- [Connect from Amazon Quick](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-managed-byo-fmkb.md): You can connect a managed Amazon Bedrock knowledge base to Amazon Quick to use it as a knowledge source.
- [Connect from AgentCore Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-gateway-target.md): Expose your Amazon Bedrock managed knowledge base as a Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool through AgentCore Gateway, so any MCP-compatible agent can retrieve from it.
- [Supported Regions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-managed-regions.md): Regions where you can create a managed Amazon Bedrock knowledge base, and feature differences in AWS GovCloud (US-West).
- [Service quotas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-managed-quotas.md): Default quotas and limits for managed Amazon Bedrock knowledge bases.

### [Ingest changes directly into a knowledge base](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-direct-ingestion.md)

Learn how to use the KnowledgeBaseDocuments API operations to modify and ingest documents directly.

- [Prerequisites for direct ingestion](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-direct-ingestion-prereq.md): To use direct ingestion, an IAM role must have permissions to use the KnowledgeBaseDocs API operations.
- [Ingest documents directly into a knowledge base](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-direct-ingestion-add.md): Learn how to add and ingest documents directly.
- [View information about documents in your data source](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-direct-ingestion-view.md): Learn how to view information about documents in your data source.
- [Delete documents from a knowledge base directly](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-direct-ingestion-delete.md): Learn how to delete directly.
- [View information about a data source](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-ds-info.md): Learn how to view important information about a data source for an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base, such as the current settings and sync history.
- [Modify a data source](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-ds-update.md): Learn how to change, edit, modify, or update a data source for an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base.
- [Delete a data source](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-ds-delete.md): Learn how to remove or delete a data source from an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base.

### [Build a knowledge base for multimodal content](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-multimodal.md)

Learn how to build, configure, and query knowledge bases with images, audio, and video content.

- [Choosing your processing approach](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-multimodal-choose-approach.md): Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases offers two approaches for processing multimodal content: Nova Multimodal Embeddings for visual similarity searches, and Bedrock Data Automation (BDA) for text-based processing of multimedia content.
- [Prerequisites](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-multimodal-prerequisites.md): Learn the required prerequisites before you can create a multimodal knowledge base.
- [Create a knowledge base](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-multimodal-create.md): You can create multimodal knowledge bases using either the console or API.
- [Add data sources and ingest](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-multimodal-add-data-source-and-ingest.md): After creating your knowledge base, add data sources containing your multimodal content and start ingestion jobs to process and index the content.
- [Test and query knowledge base](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-multimodal-test-and-query.md): After ingesting your multimodal content, you can test and query your knowledge base using the console or API.
- [Troubleshooting](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-multimodal-troubleshooting.md): This section provides guidance for resolving common issues encountered when working with multimodal knowledge bases.

### [Model evaluation task types](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-evaluation-tasks.md)

Learn more about the available evaluation tasks in Amazon Bedrock.

- [General text generation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-evaluation-tasks-general-text.md): General text generation is a task used by applications that include chatbots.
- [Text summarization](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-evaluation-tasks-text-summary.md): Text summarization is used for tasks including creating summaries of news, legal documents, academic papers, content previews, and content curation.
- [Question and answer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-evaluation-tasks-question-answer.md): Question and answer is used for tasks including generating automatic help-desk responses, information retrieval, and e-learning.
- [Text classification](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-evaluation-text-classification.md): Text classification is used to categorize text into pre-defined categories.
- [Prompt datasets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-evaluation-prompt-datasets.md): Learn more about using prompt datasets in model evaluation jobs
- [Create job](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-evaluation-jobs-management-create.md): Learn more about starting an automatic model evaluation job
- [List job](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-evaluation-jobs-management-list.md): Learn more how to see a list of your current automatic model evaluation jobs
- [Stop job](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-evaluation-jobs-management-stop.md): Learn more about how to stop a model evaluation job
- [Delete job](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-evaluation-jobs-management-delete.md): Learn how to remove model evaluation jobs that are no longer needed from your Amazon Bedrock account.

### [Data management and encryption in Amazon Bedrock evaluation job](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/evaluation-data-management.md)

Learn how Amazon Bedrock manages and encrypts data during model evaluation jobs to maintain security and privacy.

- [Key policy requirements](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-evaluation-security-kms.md): Every AWS KMS key must have exactly one key policy.
- [IAM policy requirements](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-evaluation-security-data.md): Amazon Bedrock uses the following IAM and AWS KMS permissions to use your AWS KMS key to decrypt your files and access them.
- [Data encryption for knowledge base evaluation jobs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/rag-evaluation-security-data.md): During a knowledge base evaluation job, Amazon Bedrock makes a temporary copy of your data.
- [Management events](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-events-in-model-evaluations.md): Learn about AWS CloudTrail management events generated during Amazon Bedrock model evaluation jobs for auditing and monitoring.

- [Create a session](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/sessions-create.md): Create a session
- [Store conversation history and context in a session](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/sessions-store-coversation.md): Learn how to upload state checkpoints, including text and images, to your session
- [Retrieve conversation history and context from a session](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/sessions-retrieve-coversation.md): Learn how to retrieve state checkpoints, including text and images, from your session
- [End a session when the user ends the conversation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/sessions-end-session.md): Learn how to end a session when the user ends the conversation.
- [Delete a session and all of its data](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/sessions-delete-session.md): Learn how to delete a session and all of its data.
- [Manage sessions with BedrockSessionSaver LangGraph library](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/sessions-opensource-library.md): Learn how to store and retrieve conversation history and context in LangGraph with the BedrockSessionSaver library.

## [References/Advanced](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/references.md)

- [Key terminology](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/key-definitions.md): Learn essential generative AI and Amazon Bedrock terminology to understand foundation models, model inference, and advanced features.
- [API reference overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/api-reference-overview.md): Overview of the Amazon Bedrock API reference, including endpoints, CLI references, and SDK references.

### [Using models with Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/foundation-models-reference.md)

A foundation model is an Artificial Intelligence model with a large number of parameters and trained on a massive amount of diverse data.

- [Supported models](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/models-supported.md): Information previously on this page, including model IDs, supported Regions, modalities, and inference parameters, has moved to models at a glance.
- [Model support by Region](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/models-regions.md): Information previously on this page has moved.
- [Feature support by Region](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/features-regions.md): Information previously on this page has moved.
- [Model support by feature](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/models-features.md): Information previously on this page has moved.
- [Working with AWS SDKs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/sdk-general-information-section.md): Provides links to AWS SDK developer guides and to code example folders (on GitHub) to help interested customers quickly find the information they need to start building applications.
- [API Error Codes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/troubleshooting-api-error-codes.md): Learn about common Amazon Bedrock API errors, their causes, and how to resolve them when using Amazon Bedrock services.

### [Inference parameters](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-parameters.md)

- [Amazon Titan Embeddings G1 - Text](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-parameters-titan-embed-text.md): Titan Embeddings G1 - Text does not support the use of inference parameters.

This section provides inference parameters and code examples for using the Anthropic Claude Messages API.

- [Thinking encryption](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/claude-messages-thinking-encryption.md): Full thinking content is encrypted and returned in the signature field.
- [Differences in thinking across model versions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/claude-messages-thinking-differences.md): Understand the key differences in extended thinking capabilities between Anthropic Claude 3.7 Sonnet and Claude 4 models, including output format and redaction handling.
- [Request and Response](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-parameters-anthropic-claude-messages-request-response.md): The request body is passed in the body field of a request to InvokeModel or InvokeModelWithResponseStream.
- [Code examples](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/api-inference-examples-claude-messages-code-examples.md): The following code examples show how to use the messages API.

### [Stability AI models](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-parameters-stability-diffusion.md)

- [Stable Image Ultra](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-parameters-diffusion-stable-ultra-text-image-request-response.md): The request body is passed in the body field of a request to InvokeModel operation.
- [Stable Diffusion 3.5 Large](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-parameters-diffusion-3-5-large.md): The Stable Diffusion 3.5 Large model uses 8 billion parameters and supports 1 megapixel resolution output for text-to-image and image-to-image generation.
- [Stable Image Core](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-parameters-diffusion-stable-image-core-text-image-request-response.md): The request body is passed in the body field of a request to InvokeModel.
- [Stability AI Image Services](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/stable-image-services.md): You can use Stability AI Image Services with Amazon Bedrock to access thirteen specialized image editing tools designed to accelerate professional creative workflows.

- [Supported Regions/SDKs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/api-keys-supported.md): Learn what Regions support Amazon Bedrock API keys.
- [Generate an API key](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/api-keys-generate.md): Generate and configure API keys in Amazon Bedrock to authenticate your API requests.
- [Use an API key](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/api-keys-use.md): Use an Amazon Bedrock API key to authenticate your API requests.
- [Modify permissions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/api-keys-modify.md): Learn how to modify permissions for Amazon Bedrock API keys by managing IAM policies.

- [Control permissions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/api-keys-permissions.md): Learn how to control permissions for generation and use of Amazon Bedrock API keys.

### [Manage subscriptions with License Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/managed-entitlements.md)

Learn how to centrally manage third-party Bedrock model subscriptions and distribute access across your AWS Organization.

- [Workflow overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/managed-entitlements-workflow.md): Step 1 - Subscribe: Subscribe to a third-party Bedrock serverless model through AWS Marketplace (either via auto-enablement or private offer).
- [Key concepts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/managed-entitlements-key-concepts.md)
- [Prerequisites](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/managed-entitlements-prerequisites.md): Before you can use managed entitlements for Amazon Bedrock, you must complete the following prerequisites.
- [Setup](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/managed-entitlements-setup.md): Complete the following setup steps once for your AWS Organization.
- [Subscribing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/managed-entitlements-subscribing.md): Before you can distribute licenses, you must first subscribe to a Bedrock model through AWS Marketplace.
- [Distributing licenses](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/managed-entitlements-distributing.md): After you have subscribed to a third-party Bedrock model and verified that a license has been created, you can create grants to distribute access to other accounts in your organization.
- [Accepting and activating grants](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/managed-entitlements-accepting.md): After a grant has been distributed to a member account, the grant must be accepted and activated before the third-party Bedrock model can be used.
- [Using models](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/managed-entitlements-using-models.md): Once a grant has been activated in your account, you can invoke the third-party Bedrock model using the Amazon Bedrock console, AWS CLI, or AWS SDKs.
- [Managing grants](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/managed-entitlements-managing.md): After creating grants, you may need to modify, deactivate, or delete them based on changing organizational needs.
- [API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/managed-entitlements-api.md): This section provides comprehensive API documentation for programmatically managing Managed Entitlements for Bedrock.
- [Troubleshooting](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/managed-entitlements-troubleshooting.md): This section provides solutions to common issues you may encounter when using Managed Entitlements for Amazon Bedrock.
- [FAQ](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/managed-entitlements-faq.md)
